title: KV cache precision sampling & holdout benchmark: stochastic FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: run a focused set of experiments that evaluate stochastic and sampling-based calibration strategies for KV cache quantization (INT8 and FP8) with an explicit holdout benchmarking workflow. We want to surface latency/quality trade-offs across realistic sequence length distributions and batching configurations, produce a reproducible calibration pipeline, and deliver clear pass/fail criteria for production adoption.

We will compare: (A) baseline FP16 KV cache, (B) INT8 per-layer symmetric quant with global scale, (C) FP8 exponent/mantissa variants with stochastic rounding and dynamic clip, and (D) mixed-mode profiles where keys use INT8 and values use FP8. The novelty: a sampling-based calibration harness that continuously selects calibration shards from production-like traffic and a "holdout" set kept frozen for final validation to prevent overfitting calibration to calibration-set artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible calibration pipeline checked into repo with CLI to generate profiles from a given calibration shard URL

Benchmarks comparing FP16 vs INT8 vs FP8 vs mixed profiles on the holdout set with P50/P95 token latency, relative token-per-second, and quality metrics (perplexity + EM/F1 for QA), published to the project dashboard
A decision doc recommending a candidate profile (or profiles) for further canarying based on the 3x axes: latency improvement, unit-cost reduction, and max allowed quality regression
If selected profile causes >5% regression on primary QA metric or >2.5x variance on rollout stability, mark as not production-ready and list mitigations
steps: Design calibration sample strategy: stratified sampling by sequence length (short/medium/long) and by model stage (prefill/streaming). Produce 10 shards of ~5k requests each (dev-only).
Implement calibration harness: sampling, per-layer histogram collection, scale optimization job, and profile exporter (json).
Integrate stochastic rounding and clip annealing knobs into runtime quantization patch (branch: feature/kv-stochastic-quant).

Run grid sweep across temperature of stochastic rounding, per-layer vs per-tensor scale, and FP8 exponent bias. Use a small synthetic sweep on dev cluster first (g5x2), then larger cluster (A100) for final runs.
Evaluate on frozen holdout: measure P50/P95 token latency, mean tokens/sec, perplexity delta, QA EM/F1, and embedding cosine similarity. Produce per-sequence-length breakdowns.
Produce comparison report and recommendation; if profile passes, prepare canary rollout plan with rollback gates and telemetry to monitor latency/quality drift.
metrics: Latency: token-level P50 and P95 (ms), end-to-end request latency (ms)
Throughput: tokens/sec normalized to FP16 baseline
Quality: perplexity relative delta, QA EM and F1 on holdout, embedding cosine mean/95th percentile
Stability: variance of token latency across 30-minute windows during load
Cost proxy: GPU-seconds per 1M tokens and estimated $/1M tokens
notes: We intentionally keep a frozen holdout to avoid calibration overfitting — this was a recurring issue in last quarter's sweep.
Primary focus for adoption is production Dedicated customers with long chat sessions where KV cache dominates token cost.
If mixed profile (keys INT8 + values FP8) looks promising, we need a follow-up to adapt cache reconciliation and migration logic in runtime.
